newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN torture body writes Israel to express concern.
newsitem.headline: UN torture body writes Israel to express concern.

text.p: The U.N. Committee against Torture said on Friday it was writing to the Israeli government expressing concern that a recent ruling by Israel's High Court appeared to violate the 1987 Convention against Torture.
A U.N. source told Reuters: "The letter requests an answer from the Israeli government."
A week ago, Israel's High Court overturned an interim court order which had forbidden Israel's Shin Bet secret police using "physical force" against a Palestinian detainee.

The U.N. Committee against Torture, which ended its semi-annual session in Geneva on Friday, oversees compliance with the 1987 convention, signed by 100 states. Israel ratified it in 1991, but made certain stipulations.

Peter Burns, a Canadian expert on the U.N. body and its rapporteur for Israel, said: "We can sympathise with the situation Israel confronts, everybody I think must. But it is clear that the ends never justify the means."
